comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE (AC-1) — why the layered guards passed the laundered tag on epic fb8a-7363-e406-4e36:

(1) evidence-kind DID run and returned nothing. The retag-then-PASS review is the execution-phase run reviewed_at=1786735661266802001 (latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar on fb8a, verdict PASS, review_phase=execution). Its coverage.routing.agent_tier list INCLUDES evidence-kind and llm_ran=true — routing, the .rebar overlay, and the execution phase were all NOT the defect. But the run's findings contain no evidence-kind finding at all (findings criteria: E1, G4, T12, P5, P6, T5e, G4) despite AC-19's tagged text citing tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py verbatim — an LLM judgment miss with no deterministic backstop. (Blocking would have been available: block_threshold 0.95, default_posture blocking, execution floor 0.80.)

(2) det_measurement_provenance DID detect both tagged ACs' missing provenance lines — the run's P6 finding f607dd457c67f9209 carries the exact two gaps in its evidence — but that lint is wired into p6_ac_quality, which is ADVISORY by contract ('p6 never blocks'), so it surfaced as coaching and the verdict stayed PASS.

(3) At close, txn.ensure_ac_boxes_checked exempts tagged items at face value and the completion verifier classifies solely from the author tag (ADR-0043, by design). No deterministic close-path guard existed. Net: every layer either trusted the tag by contract or was advisory; the only blocking-capable layer was a nondeterministic LLM judgment.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIX (design decisions): deterministic, fail-closed, pre-LLM, on the close path — the point the ticket names as the rejection point since the verifier must keep trusting the tag (ADR-0043).

- New pure detector src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_attestation_launder.py: laundering_gaps() fires per [operator-attested] AC item whose own block (checkbox line + indented continuation lines, bounded by the next checkbox or the AC section end) cites exact repo path/symbol evidence. Precision-first matchers: repo-root-anchored paths (src|tests|docs|scripts/...), slash paths with a code extension incl. pytest ::node ids, bare test_* symbols; URLs scrubbed first. Commit hashes and Gerrit change numbers deliberately do NOT fire — they are the attestation-EVENT provenance ADR-0043's contract itself demands (this is what keeps AC-4's legitimate escape hatch working).
- New close guard txn.ensure_attested_items_valid, wired into close_precheck._completion_precheck right after ensure_ac_boxes_checked: (a) laundering → block with untag/split remedy (reported FIRST so the author is never coached into decorating a mistag with provenance); (b) missing/incomplete provenance: line → block (det_measurement_provenance.provenance_gaps promoted to blocking on the close path only; review-side P6 stays advisory by contract). --force bypasses upstream as with every close precheck; unreadable tickets silently pass (other guards own that).
- SCOPE decision: the guard scans the AC item's own text/continuation lines, NOT ticket comments — every real ticket's progress comments cite repo paths, so comment-scanning would false-positive universally.
- Updated 3 lifecycle tests that pinned the face-value exemption (they now carry valid provenance lines); doc section added to docs/plan-review-gate.md.

Evidence: RED first (mistagged + missing-provenance fixtures reached the billable verifier on clean HEAD), then GREEN. 29 new tests across tests/unit/test_det_attestation_launder.py, tests/unit/test_attested_close_guard.py, tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_close_guard_e2e.py. Mutation pass: 12/12 mutants killed (invert tag detection, skip URL scrub, drop each matcher, whole-section scan, containment filter, skip either check, unwire precheck, boundary errors). make lint + typecheck + complexity ratchet clean; lifecycle suite 591 passed; close/precheck/attest unit slice 569 passed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PS2 assessment of the 7-day failure-mining signals against change 1791:

RISK 1 (mixed-evidence false positives) — CONFIRMED and fixed. Empirical check on the PS1 guard: (a) a tagged AC whose provenance declares external evidence but whose prose names a repo path for ORIENTATION ("the fix shipped in src/rebar/_store/sync.py is deployed to prod") falsely fired. (b) A genuinely MIXED criterion (test file cited as the repo-verifiable half + external exit-code outcome) fired — that one is intended policy: SPLIT.

PS2 detector change (det_attestation_launder.py): citations are now judged per-line with an evidence-vs-orientation rule. Test-shaped citations (tests/ paths, test_* segments/symbols, pytest ::node ids) ALWAYS fire — a test is inherently completion proof, never orientation. Other repo citations (src/, docs/, code-extension slash paths) fire only when an evidence-introducing word (proxy/proof/evidence/verified/covered/documented/...) precedes them on the same line. URLs scrubbed first; commit SHAs / Gerrit numbers still never fire (ADR-0043 provenance). The block message now explicitly coaches the SPLIT for mixed criteria: cited paths/symbols move to a new UNTAGGED criterion; the external outcome keeps the tag with its provenance line.

RISK 2 (f680 catch-22) — evaluated, exemption NOT implemented, deliberately. Normalizing [operator-attested] tag edits out of the plan-review material fingerprint is not a small contained change (it touches the signed-hash contract), and a direction-insensitive exemption would let post-certification RETAGGING escape attestation invalidation — the exact laundering vector this bug closes (fb8a's re-review only happened BECAUSE the retag staled the attestation). Mitigation shipped instead: both block messages now state that the untag/split/provenance edit stales the signed plan-review attestation and to expect re-running rebar review-plan, so the re-review cycle is documented, not a surprise. Follow-up recommendation: if a DIRECTION-SENSITIVE seam is ever designed (tag-REMOVE + provenance-line-ADD exempt; tag-ADD always material), that could safely cut the two extra review cycles — file it as its own ticket with a signing-contract review.

PS2 validation: 9 new tests (orientation no-fire, mixed fires + split coaching, marker-position pin, cross-line dedupe, URL-scrub-at-laundering-level, bare-test-symbol, staleness message x2); 8/8 new-logic mutants killed (incl. one survivor N8 — URL scrub in the per-line path — killed by a new test); make lint + typecheck + complexity ratchet clean; targeted suites 56 passed; broad unit suite 2157 passed (only known-environmental failures).

## Problem
The layered defenses against the attestation-laundering anti-pattern — tagging a CODE-VERIFIABLE acceptance criterion `[operator-attested]` so the completion verifier accepts a ticket comment instead of repository proof — failed to reject a live instance.

## Reproduction (today, epic fb8a-7363-e406-4e36 close)
1. Epic close failed: completion verifier hit its step budget (request_limit=24) and reported AC-19 unmet — though its proof is repo-resident (tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py::test_fsck_default_skips_archived_and_flag_restores et al., merged 39de64871c).
2. The operator retagged AC-19 `[operator-attested]` (the anti-pattern; a misclassification — the evidence is an exact path/symbol repository fact).
3. `rebar review-plan fb8a-7363-e406-4e36` → PASS. Expected: the evidence-kind criterion (criteria_routing.json "FIRE on … a tagged repository fact grounded by exact path/symbol evidence") fires; also the AC carried NO `provenance:` continuation line, which det_measurement_provenance (plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py) is supposed to require on every tagged AC.
4. Close succeeded: the completion verifier accepted the tag at face value — correct per its prompt (completion_verifier.md "How you classify a criterion: SOLELY from an author tag"; ADR-0043 makes the tag a trust escape hatch), which is exactly why the REVIEW-side guards must be the rejection point.

## Suspected defects (investigate all)
- Evidence-kind criterion did not fire on a tagged repo-provable AC at re-review time (routing overlay not applied? criterion advisory instead of blocking? re-review of an in_progress ticket skips it?).
- det_measurement_provenance did not flag the missing `provenance:` line (same questions; det_floor.py wiring says ADVISORY — if so, advisory is insufficient for this class).
- Consider a deterministic pre-close guard: a criterion whose text cites an exact repo path/symbol (or whose evidence comment does) but carries the tag is auto-rejected before any LLM runs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Root cause identified for why the plan-review evidence-kind guard passed a tagged repository fact (with the failing review run cited).
- [x] A mistagged code-verifiable AC (repo path/symbol evidence exists) is REJECTED before close: reproduced RED with a fixture ticket, then GREEN after the fix.
- [x] A tagged AC missing its `provenance:` continuation line is rejected (or the advisory is promoted to blocking for close-path reviews), with tests.
- [x] Legitimately external ACs (deploy/vote/console evidence with provenance) still pass: guard test.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
